refs.ar: إِذْ قَالَ اللَّهُ يَا عِيسَىٰ إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا
refs.en: When Allah said, “O Jesus, I will cause you to die (a natural death), and will exalt you to Myself, and will clear you of the charges of those who disbelieve…”

refs.ar: قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: مُتَوَفِّيكَ: مُمِيتُكَ
refs.en: Ibn Abbas said: mutawaffika means “I will cause you to die.”
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tafsir, Surah al-Ma’idah

k1.use:
Short version: “Allah told Jesus: ‘I will cause you to die and raise you to Me.’ Death comes first. The Prophet’s own cousin Ibn Abbas translated it as ‘I will cause you to die’ — it is in Sahih Bukhari.”

Then ask: “Can you show me one place in the Quran or Arabic where Allah is the subject, a person is the object, and tawaffa means lifting the body alive to heaven?”
k1.gr:
• مُتَوَفِّيكَ is the active participle (ism fa’il) of تَوَفَّى (Form V, bab tafa’ul).
• When Allah is the subject (fa’il) and a human being the object (maf’ul bihi), tawaffa always means taking the soul — i.e. death, or sleep only when sleep/night is explicitly mentioned (39:43, 6:61).
• The و (waw) normally keeps the stated order; claims of “taqdim wa ta’khir” (reversed order) are an assumption with no indication (qarina) in the verse.

obj.o: “Mutawaffika means ‘I will take you in full (body and soul)’.”
obj.a: Then the same word must mean that for the Holy Prophet (sa) in 10:47 (10:46) and for Yusuf’s prayer “tawaffani musliman” (12:102 / 12:101) — nobody says those mean being lifted bodily. Ibn Abbas explicitly said it means death.

obj.o: “The order is reversed: raised first, death later.”
obj.a: There is no indication (qarina) in the verse for reversing the order. If the order of the first two is reversed, why not the other promises too? Also see the site page “Imam Razi: explanation of taqdeem wa takhir”.

refs.ar: وَكُنتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًا مَّا دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ ۖ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي كُنتَ أَنتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ
refs.en: “…and I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them, but since You caused me to die, You have been the Watcher over them.”

refs.ar: فَأَقُولُ كَمَا قَالَ الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: وَكُنتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًا مَا دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي
refs.en: The Holy Prophet (sa): “Then I will say as the righteous servant (Jesus) said: ‘I was a witness over them while I was among them; but when You caused me to die…’”
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tafsir, Surah al-Ma’idah

k2.use: Ask: “Has the Christian creed been corrupted already? Yes. Jesus says it got corrupted after Allah ‘tawaffa’ him. So he has already been ‘tawaffa’d’. And the Prophet (sa) used the same word for his own death in Bukhari.”
k2.gr:
• تَوَفَّيْتَنِي: past tense, Allah (you) is the subject and Jesus (me) the object — the same pattern that means death throughout the Quran.
• The Holy Prophet (sa) applied the identical word to himself, and for him it can only mean death. One word, same speaker-pattern, same meaning.

obj.o: “Tawaffaytani here means ‘You raised me up alive’.”
obj.a: Then the Prophet’s (sa) use of the same sentence would mean he was raised alive bodily — which no Muslim believes. The Prophet (sa) said “as the righteous servant said” — same words, same meaning.

refs.ar: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ ۚ أَفَإِن مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَىٰ أَعْقَابِكُمْ
refs.en: “And Muhammad is only a Messenger. Verily, all Messengers have passed away before him. If then he die or be slain, will you turn back on your heels?”
Abu Bakr (ra) recited this verse after the Prophet’s death; the people felt as if they had never heard it before, and everyone began reciting it.
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Maghazi, Bab Marad al-Nabi wa Wafatihi

k3.use: Story-first: tell the scene of Umar (ra) with his sword and Abu Bakr (ra) reciting the verse. Then: “If even one prophet was alive in heaven, the argument fails. Every Companion accepted it — the first ijma in Islam.”
k3.gr:
• الرُّسُلُ has the definite article al- (lam al-istighraq) = all the messengers, without exception.
• The verse itself defines how they “passed away”: أَفَإِن مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ — either natural death or being killed. There is no third option (ascending alive).
• خَلَا is used in Arabic for passing away/dying (see site pages “Khala from dictionaries”, “Sharh Diwan Hamasa”).

obj.o: “Khalat only means ‘came and went’, not died.”
obj.a: The verse explains it right away: “if he dies or is killed”. And Abu Bakr used it to prove a death.

refs.ar: مَّا الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ ۖ كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ الطَّعَامَ
refs.en: “The Messiah, son of Mary, was only a Messenger; surely, Messengers like him had passed away before him. And his mother was a truthful woman. They both used to eat food.”

refs.ar: وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُمْ جَسَدًا لَّا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوا خَالِدِينَ
refs.en: “Nor did We give them bodies that ate no food, nor were they to live for ever.”

k4.use: “Mary has died — everyone agrees. The Quran puts Jesus in the same sentence: ‘they both used to eat.’ And 21:9 says prophets are not given bodies that live without food.”
k4.gr:
• كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ = kana + imperfect verb = a past continuous habit (“they used to eat”) that is no longer the case.
• Jesus and Mary are joined in one verb: whatever applies to Mary’s eating (she has died) applies to Jesus.

refs.ar: وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ ۖ أَفَإِن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ
refs.en: “We granted not everlasting life to any human being before you. If then you should die, shall they live here for ever?”

k5.use: “Is Jesus a human (bashar)? Yes. Did he come before the Prophet? Yes. Then this verse includes him.”
k5.gr:
• لِبَشَرٍ is indefinite after a negation (nakira fi siyaq al-nafi) = it covers every single human without exception.
• الْخُلْد here means a very long/abiding life, contrasted with the Prophet’s (sa) death in the same verse.

refs.ar: وَجَعَلَنِي مُبَارَكًا أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُ وَأَوْصَانِي بِالصَّلَاةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّا
refs.en: “And He has made me blessed wherever I may be, and has enjoined upon me Prayer and almsgiving as long as I live.”

k6.use: Light, memorable question: “Who are the poor in heaven that he gives Zakat to?”
k6.gr:
• مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّا — “ma dumtu” = for as long as; the obligation lasts exactly as long as his life.
• Compare 5:118: مَا دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ — same construction, used for the time he was among his people.

refs.ar: أَوْ تَرْقَىٰ فِي السَّمَاءِ ... قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّي هَلْ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرًا رَّسُولًا
refs.en: “…or you ascend into heaven… Say, ‘Holy is my Lord! I am but a man sent as a Messenger.’”

k7.use: “If ascending bodily were possible for a prophet, why did the best of prophets refuse, saying ‘I am only a human’?”

refs.ar: بَل رَّفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا
refs.en: “On the contrary, Allah exalted him to Himself. And Allah is Mighty, Wise.”

refs.ar: وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَرَفَعْنَاهُ بِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّهُ أَخْلَدَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ
refs.en: “If We had pleased, We could have exalted him thereby; but he inclined to the earth.”

refs.ar: يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجَاتٍ
refs.en: “Allah will raise those who believe among you and those who are given knowledge, to degrees of rank.”

refs.ar: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَارْحَمْنِي وَاجْبُرْنِي وَارْزُقْنِي وَارْفَعْنِي
refs.en: Prayer between the two prostrations: “…and raise me (warfa’ni).” Every Muslim asks this — no one means bodily lifting.
refs.cite: Sunan Ibn Majah, Kitab Iqamat al-Salat

k8.use: “When you pray ‘warfa’ni’ between the sajdas, do you expect to float up? Then why make it mean that for Jesus?”
k8.gr:
• رَفَعَ with a person as object and Allah as subject = raising in rank/honour (7:177, 58:12, 19:58 for Idris).
• إِلَيْهِ (“to Himself”) — Allah is not confined to the sky. Compare Ibrahim: إِنِّي ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي “I am going to my Lord” (37:100 / 37:99), meaning migration, not ascending.

obj.o: “The word ‘bal’ (rather) shows he was lifted up instead of being killed.”
obj.a: ‘Bal’ contrasts the accursed death (crucifixion) with honour and nearness to Allah — which is exactly what the Jews denied. It does not specify the sky.

refs.ar: وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ
refs.en: “…whereas they slew him not, nor crucified him (to death), but he was made to appear to them like one crucified.”

refs.ar: وَآوَيْنَاهُمَا إِلَىٰ رَبْوَةٍ ذَاتِ قَرَارٍ وَمَعِينٍ
refs.en: “And We gave them refuge on an elevated land of green valleys and springs of running water.”
“For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.” — Jonah entered alive and came out alive.

k9.use: With Christians: use the sign of Jonah — alive in, alive out. With Muslims: “Who was the innocent man punished in his place? Where does the Quran mention him?”
k9.gr:
• صَلَبَ in Arabic means to kill by crucifixion, not merely to hang on a cross (see “Lisan al-Arab: meaning of salaba”).
• شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ — passive: “it (the matter) was made doubtful/similar for them”. The verse does not mention any other person being substituted; the substitution theory is refuted even by Imam Razi (see Related).

obj.o: “Someone else (Judas etc.) was made to look like Jesus.”
obj.a: The Quran never says this. It would mean Allah deceived everyone, including Mary and the disciples, and punished an innocent person. Imam Razi and Abu Hayyan (Bahr al-Muhit) criticised this theory (see site references).

refs.ar: وَآوَيْنَاهُمَا إِلَىٰ رَبْوَةٍ ذَاتِ قَرَارٍ وَمَعِينٍ
refs.en: “And We gave them refuge on an elevated land of green valleys and springs of running water.”
“I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
“And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring.”

k10.use: Book reference: Jesus in India by the Promised Messiah (as). Site pages: “The Rozabal Line: Yuz Asaf prophet’s grave”, “Rashid Rida: Jesus going to India is not far-fetched”.
k10.gr: • آوَيْنَا (from إيواء) = to give shelter/refuge after hardship — not a description of his birth.

refs.ar: إِنَّ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ عَاشَ عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةَ سَنَةٍ
refs.en: “Jesus son of Mary lived for one hundred and twenty years.”

k11.use: “The Prophet (sa) spoke of Jesus’ life in the past tense with a complete number of years.”
k11.gr: • عَاشَ is past tense: he “lived” — a completed life.

refs.ar: لَوْ كَانَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ حَيَّيْنِ لَمَا وَسِعَهُمَا إِلَّا اتِّبَاعِي
refs.en: “If Moses and Jesus were alive, they would have no choice but to follow me.”
refs.cite: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (under 3:82 / 3:81); al-Yawaqit wal-Jawahir; Madarij al-Salikin (Ibn Qayyim)

k12.use: Pair it with the Mi’raj: the Prophet (sa) saw Jesus with Yahya (as) — who had died — among the souls of the prophets (Sahih Bukhari, hadith of the Mi’raj).
k12.gr: • لَوْ (law) introduces a hypothetical that did not happen (harf imtina’ li-imtina’): “if they were alive (they are not)…”.

refs.ar: اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِهَا
refs.en: “Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that die not, during their sleep.”

refs.ar: وَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ
refs.en: “Whether We show you some of what We promise them, or cause you to die…” — said to the Holy Prophet (sa).

refs.ar: تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ
refs.en: Yusuf’s prayer: “Let me die in submission and join me with the righteous.”

k13.use: Make it a challenge, politely: “Show me one example — just one — where Allah does tawaffa of a person and it means taking the body to heaven.”
k13.gr:
• Form V verb تَوَفَّى from the root و ف ي (to complete). Object of the verb is the soul (al-anfus) — even in 39:43 what is taken is the nafs, not the body.
• Sleep is only meant when a qarina is given: فِي مَنَامِهَا (39:43), بِاللَّيْلِ (6:61). No such qarina in 3:56 or 5:118.
• Classical lexicons (e.g. Lisan al-Arab, Taj al-Arus) give قبض الروح (taking the soul) as its meaning with Allah as subject.
• The Promised Messiah (as) publicly challenged anyone to produce a counter-example from the Quran, Hadith or classical Arabic (Izala-e-Auham); no one did.

refs.ar: كَيْفَ أَنتُمْ إِذَا نَزَلَ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ فِيكُمْ وَإِمَامُكُمْ مِنكُمْ
refs.en: “How will you be when the son of Mary descends among you, and he will be your Imam from among you.”
“And if ye will receive it, this is Elias (Elijah), which was for to come.”
refs.cite: Matthew 11:14 (cf. Malachi 4:5; Luke 1:17 “in the spirit and power of Elias”)

refs.en: The Holy Prophet (sa) described the earlier Jesus as reddish with curly hair, and the coming Messiah as wheat-coloured with straight hair — two different people.

k14.use: With Christians: Elijah/John the Baptist precedent. With Muslims: “Two different descriptions in Bukhari = two different people.”
k14.gr:
• نَزَلَ (nuzul) is used in the Quran for things that come from Allah but are made on earth: clothing (7:27), iron (57:26), cattle (39:7), the Prophet himself (65:11-12). It means an honoured arrival, not falling from the sky.
• إِمَامُكُمْ مِنكُمْ — “your Imam from among you”: he arises from within the Muslims.

refs.ar: تَوَفَّاهُ اللّٰهُ: قَبَضَ رُوحَهُ
refs.en: “Allah did tawaffa of him” = He took his soul.
refs.cite: Al-Qamus; Taj al-Arus; Lisan al-Arab (under و ف ي); Sihah al-Jawhari

refs.ar: حِينَ تُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللّٰهِ ﷺ ... فَقُلْتُ لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ: تَوَفَّى اللّٰهُ نَبِيَّهُ
refs.en: Uthman (ra): when the Messenger of Allah died… I said to Abu Bakr, “Allah has caused His Prophet to die (tawaffa).”
refs.cite: Kanz al-Ummal (narration of Uthman, as cited in the Pocket Book p. 240)

u1.use: Offer the challenge politely, then show the dictionary entry: the rule comes from the lexicons, not from Ahmadis.
u1.gr:
• Bab tafa’ul (Form V), Allah = fa’il, a living being (dhi ruh) = maf’ul → qabd al-ruh (taking the soul).
• In the Companions’ own speech, “tawaffallahu nabiyyahu” was used for the Holy Prophet’s (sa) death.

refs.ar: وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ لَا يَخْلُقُونَ شَيْئًا وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ ۝ أَمْوَاتٌ غَيْرُ أَحْيَاءٍ ۖ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ
refs.en: “Those on whom they call besides Allah create not anything, but they are themselves created. They are dead, not living; and they know not when they will be raised.”

u2.use: “Which person is worshipped most besides Allah today? Jesus. The Quran says every such one is ‘dead, not alive’.”
u2.gr:
• أَمْوَاتٌ is the plural of مَيِّت (one who has died) — see al-Munjid. The verse adds غَيْرُ أَحْيَاءٍ (“not alive”) to remove any doubt.
• يُخْلَقُونَ — “they are created”: this is about created beings (‘alam al-khalq), i.e. humans worshipped as gods.

obj.o: “Then angels and jinn would be included too.”
obj.a: They belong to ‘alam al-amr (the world of command); the verse speaks of ‘alam al-khalq. And in any case ‘every soul shall taste death’ (29:58).

refs.ar: قَالَ فِيهَا تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ
refs.en: “He said: Therein shall you live, and therein shall you die, and therefrom shall you be brought forth.”

refs.ar: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفَاتًا ۝ أَحْيَاءً وَأَمْوَاتًا
refs.en: “Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead?”

refs.ar: وَلَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَاعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
refs.en: “And for you there is an abode on the earth and a provision for a time.”

u3.use: “The Quran restricts human life to the earth. Show me the exception for Jesus.”
u3.gr: • فِيهَا (the adverbial phrase, zarf) is placed BEFORE the verb تَحْيَوْنَ. In Arabic syntax, putting it first creates restriction (hasr): “in it — and only in it — you will live.” No exception is possible.

refs.ar: وَأَوْصَانِي بِالصَّلَاةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّا
refs.en: “…and He has enjoined upon me Prayer and almsgiving as long as I live.”

u4.use: Ask these one at a time and let the listener think; they show how the belief collapses in practice.

refs.ar: وَمُبَشِّرًا بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِي مِن بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ
refs.en: “…and giving glad tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name will be Ahmad.”

u5.use: “If Jesus comes back, the Prophet (sa) is no longer ‘after’ him. Would you change ‘min ba’di’ in the Quran?”

refs.ar: فَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ إِن كُنَّا عَنْ عِبَادَتِكُمْ لَغَافِلِينَ
refs.en: “Allah is sufficient as a witness between us and you that we were quite unaware of your worship.”

u6.use: Pair with 5:118 (“I was a witness only while I was among them”).

refs.ar: لَوْ كَانَ عِيسَىٰ حَيًّا مَا وَسِعَهُ إِلَّا اتِّبَاعِي
refs.en: “If Jesus were alive, he would have no choice but to follow me.”
refs.cite: Sharh Fiqh al-Akbar, Mulla Ali Qari, p. 100 (Egyptian edition)

u7.use: Useful with Hanafi listeners — Mulla Ali Qari is a major Hanafi scholar.
u7.gr: • لَوْ = a condition that is not fulfilled: “if he were alive (he is not)”.

refs.ar: مَا مِنْ نَفْسٍ مَنْفُوسَةٍ الْيَوْمَ يَأْتِي عَلَيْهَا مِائَةُ سَنَةٍ وَهِيَ يَوْمَئِذٍ حَيَّةٌ
refs.en: “There is no living soul today upon which a hundred years will pass while it is still alive.”
refs.cite: Sahih Muslim (narrated by Jabir); Kanz al-Ummal

refs.ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ رِيحًا يَبْعَثُهَا عَلَى رَأْسِ مِائَةِ سَنَةٍ تَقْبِضُ رُوحَ كُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ
refs.en: “Allah has a wind which He sends at the head of every hundred years, taking the soul of every believer.” (Sahih in isnad)

u8.use: See also the site pages “Sahih Bukhari / Muslim / Musnad Ahmad: no one alive today will be alive in a hundred years”.

refs.ar: أَوْحَى اللّٰهُ تَعَالَى إِلَى عِيسَى: أَنْ يَا عِيسَى انْتَقِلْ مِنْ مَكَانٍ إِلَى مَكَانٍ لِئَلَّا تُعْرَفَ فَتُؤْذَى
refs.en: “Allah revealed to Jesus: O Jesus, move from one place to another lest you be recognised and harmed.”

u9.use: Pair with the Kashmir card: “Allah told Jesus to keep travelling so he wouldn’t be recognised — does someone in heaven need to hide?”

refs.ar: وَجَبَ نُزُولُهُ فِي آخِرِ الزَّمَانِ بِتَعَلُّقِهِ بِبَدَنٍ آخَرَ
refs.en: Ibn Arabi: “His descent in the latter days must be through his connection with another body.”

refs.ar: قَدْ مَاتَ عِيسَى
refs.en: “Jesus has died.”
Imam Jubba’i: Allah caused the Messiah to die and called him to Himself.
Hazrat Aisha (ra) testified that Jesus lived 120 years.
Imam Hasan (ra), in his sermon on the night Hazrat Ali (ra) was martyred: “He passed away on the night in which the soul of Jesus son of Mary was raised.”
refs.cite: Tabaqat Ibn Sa’d (see also the site page)

u10.use: Show that belief in Jesus’ death is not an Ahmadi invention; important scholars across centuries held it.

refs.ar: وَحَرَامٌ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
refs.en: “And it is forbidden for a township which We have destroyed that they shall return.”

refs.ar: أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
refs.en: “…that they never return to them.”

refs.ar: وَمِن وَرَائِهِم بَرْزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
refs.en: “…and behind them is a barrier until the day they are raised.”

u17.use: Use it after establishing his death: “Since he died, and the dead do not return, the promised ‘son of Mary’ must be someone else.”

refs.ar: مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَا أَحَدٍ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن رَّسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ
refs.en: “Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets.”

refs.ar: الْخَاتَمُ ... أَمَّا بِفَتْحِهَا فَمَعْنَاهُ أَحْسَنُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ خَلْقًا وَخُلُقًا لِأَنَّهُ ﷺ جَمَالُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ كَالْخَاتَمِ الَّذِي يُتَجَمَّلُ بِهِ
refs.en: Imam Zurqani: “Khatam with fatha means the best of the prophets in form and character, for he is the beauty of the prophets, like a ring with which one adorns oneself.”

refs.ar: كَالْخَاتَمِ لَهُمُ الَّذِي يَخْتِمُونَ بِهِ وَيَتَزَيَّنُونَ
refs.en: “Like a seal-ring for them, with which they seal and adorn themselves.”

n1.use: Start with the context: “Why would Allah answer ‘he has no sons’ with ‘he is the last’? It answers it with ‘he is the spiritual father and seal of prophets’.” Then show Zurqani.
n1.gr:
• خَاتَم (fatha on ta) = an instrument of sealing: a seal / signet ring. خَاتِم (kasra) = one who ends. The Quran’s reading is with fatha.
• In Arabic, “khatam” followed by a plural group is praise for the most perfect of that group — e.g. khatam al-shu’ara (seal of poets), khatam al-awliya (see site page “Sharh Diwan Hamasa: in Arabic last is used to praise”).
• Context: the verse begins “Muhammad is not the father of any of your men” (answering the taunt that he had no male heir, abtar). “Lakin” (but) then gives him a greater fatherhood: spiritual father of the prophets — not a closing door.

refs.ar: قُولُوا خَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَلَا تَقُولُوا لَا نَبِيَّ بَعْدَهُ
refs.en: “Say ‘Seal of the Prophets’, but do not say ‘there is no prophet after him’.”
refs.cite: Al-Durr al-Manthur, Suyuti (under 33:41); Takmila Majma’ Bihar al-Anwar

refs.ar: هَذَا نَاظِرٌ إِلَى نُزُولِ عِيسَى وَهَذَا أَيْضًا لَا يُنَافِي حَدِيثَ لَا نَبِيَّ بَعْدِي لِأَنَّهُ أَرَادَ لَا نَبِيَّ يَنْسَخُ شَرْعَهُ
refs.en: “This looks to the descent of Jesus; nor does it contradict ‘no prophet after me’, because he meant: no prophet who abrogates his law.”

n2.use: Very strong with any listener: the Mother of the Believers herself distinguished between the two statements.

refs.en: “In the view of the common people, the Holy Prophet (sa) being Khatam means his time is after the earlier prophets and he is the last prophet. But it will be clear to people of understanding that being earlier or later in time has no merit in itself…”
refs.cite: Tahdhir al-Nas, Muhammad Qasim Nanotwi, p. 3

refs.en: “Even if, supposing, a prophet were born after the time of the Holy Prophet (sa), there would still be no difference in the finality (khatamiyyat) of Muhammad.”
refs.cite: Tahdhir al-Nas, p. 25 (Kutub Khana Rahimiyya, Deoband)

n3.use: Use with Deobandi listeners: their own founder. Ask the exact page and edition to be shown — keep a scan ready (see site page “References from Tahzir ul nas”).

refs.ar: إِنَّ الرِّسَالَةَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ بِالتَّشْرِيعِ قَدِ انْقَطَعَتْ ... وَلَا نَبِيَّ، أَيْ لَا مُشَرِّعَ وَلَا شَرِيعَةَ
refs.en: “Messengership and prophethood WITH LAW-GIVING have ended… ‘no prophet’ means no law-giver and no new law.”
refs.cite: Al-Futuhat al-Makkiyyah, Ibn Arabi, vol. 2, ch. 73

refs.ar: إِذَا هَلَكَ كِسْرَى فَلَا كِسْرَى بَعْدَهُ وَإِذَا هَلَكَ قَيْصَرُ فَلَا قَيْصَرَ بَعْدَهُ
refs.en: “When Kisra perishes there will be no Kisra after him; when Caesar perishes there will be no Caesar after him.” — yet kings continued; the ‘no’ refers to that kind of rule.
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Manaqib (Bab ‘Alamat al-Nubuwwah); also Kitab Fard al-Khumus

refs.ar: لَا يَأْتِي نَبِيٌّ بَعْدَهُ يَنْسَخُ مِلَّتَهُ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ مِنْ أُمَّتِهِ
refs.en: “No prophet will come after him who abrogates his religion and is not from his Ummah.”

refs.ar: فَانْقَطَعَ حُكْمُ نُبُوَّةِ التَّشْرِيعِ بَعْدَهُ
refs.en: “After him, the order of law-bearing prophethood ended.”
refs.cite: Al-Insan al-Kamil, Abdul Karim Jili, ch. 36

n4.use: Ask: “Will Jesus come after the Holy Prophet (sa)? Will he be a prophet? Then you also accept a prophet after him — the question is only what kind.”
n4.gr:
• لَا here is لَا نَفْيِ الْكَمَال (negation of the perfect/independent kind), as in “la fata illa Ali” or “no Kisra after Kisra”: the type is negated, not every individual.
• Opponents themselves make an exception for Jesus returning as a prophet. If “la” allowed no exception at all, Jesus could not come either.

refs.ar: اللَّهُ يَصْطَفِي مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ رُسُلًا وَمِنَ النَّاسِ
refs.en: “Allah chooses Messengers from among angels and from among men.”

n5.use: “Do angels still come down with Allah’s commands? The same verb, same sentence, covers human messengers.”
n5.gr:
• يَصْطَفِي is mudari’ (imperfect) — covers present and future.
• رُسُلًا is plural: it cannot refer only to the Holy Prophet (sa) who was already present.
• Full structure: Allah chooses messengers from angels, AND chooses messengers from men — angels are still sent, so are messengers.

refs.ar: مَّا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَىٰ مَا أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّىٰ يَمِيزَ الْخَبِيثَ مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ ۗ وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُطْلِعَكُمْ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَجْتَبِي مِن رُّسُلِهِ مَن يَشَاءُ ۖ فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ
refs.en: “Allah would not leave the believers as you are until He separates the wicked from the good. Nor would Allah reveal the unseen to you, but Allah chooses of His Messengers whom He pleases. Believe then in Allah and His Messengers.”

n6.use: Read the verse slowly and ask: “Who does Allah ‘choose from His messengers’ for the believers — the verse is addressed to Muslims.”
n6.gr: • يَجْتَبِي — imperfect: He chooses (continuing). Addressed to the believers (Muslims), about a future separation of good and bad.

refs.ar: وَمَن يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ فَأُولَٰئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ وَالشُّهَدَاءِ وَالصَّالِحِينَ
refs.en: “And whoso obeys Allah and this Messenger shall be among those on whom Allah has bestowed His blessings — the Prophets, the Truthful, the Martyrs and the Righteous.”

refs.ar: قَالَ الرَّاغِبُ: مِمَّنْ أَنْعَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الْفِرَقِ الْأَرْبَعِ فِي الْمَنْزِلَةِ وَالثَّوَابِ: النَّبِيُّ بِالنَّبِيِّ وَالصِّدِّيقُ بِالصِّدِّيقِ وَالشَّهِيدُ بِالشَّهِيدِ وَالصَّالِحُ بِالصَّالِحِ
refs.en: Imam Raghib: “…in rank and reward among the four groups: the prophet with the prophet, the truthful with the truthful, the martyr with the martyr, the righteous with the righteous.”

n7.use: “If ma’a means only ‘accompanying’, then no Muslim could become a siddiq or shahid either — only stand next to them.”
n7.gr:
• مَعَ (with) here means being counted among them in rank, as in 4:147 (4:146) “fa ula’ika ma’al-mu’minin” — they are believers, not merely next to them.
• Every Muslim prays “ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim, siratal-ladhina an’amta ‘alayhim” (1:6–7) — the path of those blessed, which 4:70 defines as including the prophets.

refs.ar: يَا بَنِي آدَمَ إِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّنكُمْ يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِي ۙ فَمَنِ اتَّقَىٰ وَأَصْلَحَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ
refs.en: “O children of Adam! If Messengers come to you from among yourselves, rehearsing My Signs to you, then whoso shall fear God and do good deeds, on them shall come no fear, nor shall they grieve.”

n8.use: Point to the emphatic future “ya’tiyannakum” and ask: “Is this verse cancelled? It is addressed to all children of Adam in the final Book.”
n8.gr:
• يَأْتِيَنَّ = imperfect + heavy nun of emphasis (nun al-ta’kid), which gives a definite FUTURE meaning. إِمَّا (in + ma) brings the emphasis nun like a lam of oath (Baydawi).
• The verse is in the Quran given to the Holy Prophet (sa), addressing all humanity; it does not say “We said this in the past”.

obj.o: “This was said to the children of Adam at the beginning of creation.”
obj.a: Nothing in the verse says it is a quotation of the past; ‘ya bani Adam’ is repeated in this surah addressing people of the Prophet’s time, e.g. 7:27, 7:32.

refs.ar: وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِيثَاقَهُمْ وَمِنكَ وَمِن نُّوحٍ وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ
refs.en: “And when We took from the Prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus son of Mary.”

refs.ar: حَاصِلُ الْكَلَامِ أَنَّهُ تَعَالَى أَوْجَبَ عَلَى جَمِيعِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ الْإِيمَانَ بِكُلِّ رَسُولٍ جَاءَ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا مَعَهُمْ
refs.en: Imam Razi: “In short, Allah made it obligatory on all prophets to believe in every messenger who comes confirming what is with them.”

n9.use: “Why take the covenant ‘from you’ (minka) if the door was shut?”

refs.ar: لَوْ عَاشَ لَكَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَبِيًّا
refs.en: “Had he lived, he would have been a truthful prophet.”

refs.ar: وَهُوَ عَجِيبٌ مِنَ النَّوَوِيِّ مَعَ وُرُودِهِ عَنْ ثَلَاثَةٍ مِنَ الصَّحَابَةِ وَكَأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَظْهَرْ لَهُ تَأْوِيلُهُ
refs.en: Imam Shawkani on Nawawi’s rejection: “This is strange of Nawawi, since it is narrated from three Companions; it seems its meaning was not clear to him.”

n10.use: Key point: Surah Ahzab (khatam verse) came in 5 AH, Ibrahim died in 10 AH. “After 33:40, the Prophet himself said Ibrahim would have been a prophet.”
n10.gr:
• لَوْ marks an unfulfilled condition, but the CONSEQUENCE must be possible in itself. Compare 21:23 (21:22): “If there were gods besides Allah, (the heavens and earth) would be ruined” — ruin is possible. Likewise “would have been a prophet” shows prophethood was possible after 33:41.
• Ibrahim died in 10 AH; Surah al-Ahzab (33:41) was revealed in 5 AH.

obj.a: Mulla Ali Qari and Shawkani defended it; it has several routes from three Companions (see the site’s cards: Kanz al-Ummal, Ibn Majah, al-Asrar al-Marfu’a, Hashiyat al-Shahab, etc.).

refs.ar: الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَامَ دِينًا
refs.en: “This day have I perfected your religion for you and completed My favour upon you and chosen for you Islam as religion.”

refs.ar: ثُمَّ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ تَمَامًا عَلَى الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ وَتَفْصِيلًا لِّكُلِّ شَيْءٍ
refs.en: “Then We gave Moses the Book — completing (Our favour) on him who did good, and an explanation of all things.”

refs.ar: اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ أَنبِيَاءَ وَجَعَلَكُم مُّلُوكًا
refs.en: “Remember Allah’s favour upon you when He appointed prophets among you and made you kings.”

n11.use: “Does a completed favour stop? The Torah was ‘complete’, and still the Gospel and the Quran came after it.”

refs.ar: أَنَا الْعَاقِبُ الَّذِي لَيْسَ بَعْدَهُ نَبِيٌّ
refs.en: “I am the ‘Aqib, after whom there is no prophet.”
refs.cite: Jami’ al-Tirmidhi, Kitab al-Adab, Bab ma ja’a fi asma’ al-Nabi

refs.ar: كَانَ يُدَلِّسُ ... قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: يُخْطِئُ فِي نَحْوٍ مِنْ عِشْرِينَ حَدِيثًا عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ
refs.en: “He used to do tadlis… Ahmad said: he erred in about twenty hadiths from al-Zuhri.”
refs.cite: Mizan al-I’tidal, al-Dhahabi, under Sufyan b. ‘Uyaynah

n12.use: Don’t argue the chain first; say: “Even accepted, ‘Aqib means no law-giving prophet after him — as Ibn Arabi and Mulla Ali Qari explain.”

refs.en: “My example and the example of the prophets before me is like a man who built a house and made it beautiful, except for the place of one brick in a corner… I am that brick, and I am the seal of the prophets.”

n13.use: See also the site cards “Last Brick?” and “Musnad Ahmad: bricks of prophets”.

refs.ar: قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ عَلَىٰ فَتْرَةٍ مِّنَ الرُّسُلِ أَن تَقُولُوا مَا جَاءَنَا مِن بَشِيرٍ وَلَا نَذِيرٍ
refs.en: “There has come to you Our Messenger, after a break in (the series of) Messengers, who makes things clear to you lest you say, ‘There has come to us no bearer of glad tidings and no warner.’”

n14.use: Ask: “Why did Allah send a messenger after a long gap? So no one could say no warner came. Is our age in less need?”
n14.gr: • فَتْرَة = an interval/break: the period between Jesus and the Holy Prophet (sa) (Bahr al-Muhit). Hassan b. Thabit (ra): “A prophet came to us after despair and a break in messengers, while idols were worshipped on earth.”

refs.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ لِهَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ عَلَى رَأْسِ كُلِّ مِائَةِ سَنَةٍ مَنْ يُجَدِّدُ لَهَا دِينَهَا
refs.en: “Allah will raise for this Ummah at the head of every century one who will renew its religion.”

refs.ar: وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ كَمَا اسْتَخْلَفَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
refs.en: “Allah has promised those among you who believe and do good works that He will surely make them successors in the earth, as He made successors from among those before them.”

n15.use: Begin every Khatm-e-Nabuwwat conversation here: first make clear what we do and do not believe, so the discussion is about the real position.

refs.ar: فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُرًا مِّن قَبْلِهِ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
refs.en: “I have indeed lived among you a whole lifetime before this. Will you not then understand?”

t1.use: “The same test the Quran gives for the Holy Prophet (sa): look at his life before the claim.”

obj.o: “He said himself that nobody knew him, so who could object?”
obj.a: He wrote that he was unknown to the wider world, but the people of his own villages and the region knew him well — exactly the people the verse says can judge.

refs.ar: وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ الْأَقَاوِيلِ ۝ لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ ۝ ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ
refs.en: “And if he had forged and attributed any sayings to Us, We would surely have seized him by the right hand, and then surely We would have severed his life-artery.”

refs.ar: وَهُوَ مُسْتَمِرٌّ فِي الِافْتِرَاءِ عَلَيْهِ ثَلَاثَةً وَعِشْرِينَ سَنَةً وَهُوَ مَعَ ذَلِكَ يُؤَيِّدُهُ
refs.en: Ibn Qayyim (arguing with a Christian): How could someone keep fabricating against God for 23 years, and God still support him?

refs.ar: هَذَا هُوَ الْوَاجِبُ فِي حِكْمَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى لِئَلَّا يَشْتَبِهَ الصَّادِقُ بِالْكَاذِبِ
refs.en: Imam Razi: “This is necessary in Allah’s wisdom, so that the truthful is not confused with the liar.”

t2.use: Ask for one example: a man who falsely claimed revelation, publicly, and lived 23 years and prospered.
t2.gr:
• تَقَوَّلَ (Form V) = to fabricate sayings and attribute them falsely.
• الْوَتِين = the aorta / life-artery — a sudden, decisive destruction.

obj.o: “Yahya (John the Baptist) was killed — was he false?”
obj.a: The rule is one-way: a FALSE claimant cannot get 23 years. It does not say every true prophet lives 23 years. Even Maulvi Thanaullah noted that not everyone killed was false.

obj.o: “What about Abu al-Khattab, Ahmad b. Kayyal and other claimants?”
obj.a: Abu al-Khattab claimed divinity, not revelation, and was killed in prison in Kufa (Ibn Taymiyya, Minhaj al-Sunnah). Ahmad b. Kayyal never claimed prophethood and his followers disowned him (Ibn Hazm, al-Fasl).

refs.ar: قَالُوا يَا صَالِحُ قَدْ كُنتَ فِينَا مَرْجُوًّا قَبْلَ هَٰذَا
refs.en: “They said, ‘O Salih, you were among us one in whom we placed great hopes before this.’”

refs.ar: بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ
refs.en: “Nay, he is a boastful liar.” — what they said after the claim.

t3.use: Show Batalvi’s praise of Barahin-e-Ahmadiyya, then 11:63: the same people praise a prophet before his claim and oppose him after.

obj.o: “The Promised Messiah also misjudged people (e.g. Khwaja Kamaluddin), so Batalvi’s praise means nothing.”
obj.a: The comparison fails: Batalvi praised his character and service of Islam BEFORE the claim; the claim alone changed his view, not any change in conduct — exactly the pattern of 11:63.

refs.ar: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ ۖ قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِعَشْرِ سُوَرٍ مِّثْلِهِ مُفْتَرَيَاتٍ وَادْعُوا مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُم مِّن دُونِ اللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ
refs.en: “Do they say, ‘He has forged it’? Say, ‘Then bring ten surahs like it, forged, and call on whom you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.’”

refs.ar: قَالَ نَبِيٌّ: آيَةُ صِدْقِي أَنِّي فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ أُحَرِّكُ إِصْبَعِي وَلَا يَقْدِرُ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْبَشَرِ عَلَى مُعَارَضَتِي ... ثَبَتَ صِدْقُهُ
refs.en: Imam Ghazali: if a prophet says his sign is that he will move his finger today and no human can match it, and no one does — his truth is established. (Setting a time limit does not lessen a sign.)

t4.use: Mention I’jaz al-Masih and the reward offered; ask the listener whether any scholar answered it in the time given.

refs.ar: قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ هَادُوا إِن زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ لِلَّهِ مِن دُونِ النَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ ۝ وَلَا يَتَمَنَّوْنَهُ أَبَدًا بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ
refs.en: “Say: O you who are Jews, if you think that you are the friends of Allah to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death if you are truthful. But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent on before them.”
He invited all opposing scholars to Mubahala, writing that if every one of them was not struck by a visible calamity within a year, he would consider himself a liar.

t5.use: See also 3:62 (3:61), the verse of Mubahala with the Christians of Najran.

refs.ar: ظَهَرَ الْفَسَادُ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي النَّاسِ
refs.en: “Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what men’s hands have wrought.”

refs.ar: وَإِن كَانُوا مِن قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُّبِينٍ
refs.en: “…although they had been before in manifest error.”

t6.use: Ask: “Do you agree the Ummah is in decline today? Has Allah ever left people without guidance in such a time?” The Pocket Book quotes Muslim leaders’ own descriptions of the state of the Ummah.

refs.ar: إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ
refs.en: “Surely, the wrongdoers do not prosper.”
“I will carry your message to the ends of the earth.”
refs.cite: Revelation of the Promised Messiah (as), Tadhkirah

t7.use: Ask: “Which false claimant’s community grew in 200+ countries for over a century despite persecution?” Read 6:22.

refs.ar: عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ فَلَا يُظْهِرُ عَلَىٰ غَيْبِهِ أَحَدًا ۝ إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضَىٰ مِن رَّسُولٍ
refs.en: “He is the Knower of the unseen; and He does not grant anyone predominance over His unseen, except to a Messenger whom He chooses.”

t8.use: Give 2–3 fulfilled prophecies with dates (Lekhram 1897, Dowie 1907, eclipses 1894), then read 72:27–28.
t8.gr: • يُظْهِرُ عَلَى = to grant clear, abundant disclosure (izhar), not a passing glimpse — that is the mark of messengers.

refs.ar: وَآخَرِينَ مِنْهُمْ لَمَّا يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
refs.en: “And among others from among them who have not yet joined them. He is the Mighty, the Wise.”

refs.ar: فَوَضَعَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَدَهُ عَلَى سَلْمَانَ ثُمَّ قَالَ: لَوْ كَانَ الْإِيمَانُ عِنْدَ الثُّرَيَّا لَنَالَهُ رِجَالٌ أَوْ رَجُلٌ مِنْ هَؤُلَاءِ
refs.en: “The Messenger of Allah put his hand on Salman and said: Even if faith were at the Pleiades, men — or a man — from these would surely attain it.”
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tafsir, Surah al-Jumu’ah

refs.ar: يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ
refs.en: “He will plan the affair from the heaven to the earth, then it shall go up to Him in a day the measure of which is a thousand years according to what you reckon.” — after the first three good centuries, faith ‘rises away’ for 1,000 years, reaching the 14th century AH.

t9.use: Link: Prophet (sa) put his hand on Salman — a Persian man would bring faith back from the Pleiades. The Promised Messiah’s family was Persian (Mughal Barlas). Add 32:6: after the first three centuries, faith rises away for 1,000 years — bringing us to the 14th century.
t9.gr:
• وَآخَرِينَ is joined to الْأُمِّيِّينَ in 62:3: “He raised among the unlettered a Messenger from among them… and among others” — the same Messenger is raised among a later people (a second, spiritual advent).
• لَمَّا يَلْحَقُوا — “have not YET joined” (lamma = not yet, but will).

refs.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ لِهَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ عَلَى رَأْسِ كُلِّ مِائَةِ سَنَةٍ مَنْ يُجَدِّدُ لَهَا دِينَهَا
refs.en: “Allah will raise for this Ummah at the head of every century one who will renew its religion.”

refs.ar: الْآيَاتُ بَعْدَ الْمِائَتَيْنِ
refs.en: “The signs (will come) after the two hundred (i.e. after 1200 AH).”
refs.cite: Mishkat al-Masabih; Ibn Majah (as quoted in the Pocket Book)

t10.use: “Name the mujaddid of the 14th century. If it isn’t him, who was it?”

refs.ar: إِنَّ لِمَهْدِيِّنَا آيَتَيْنِ لَمْ تَكُونَا مُنْذُ خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: يَنْكَسِفُ الْقَمَرُ لِأَوَّلِ لَيْلَةٍ مِنْ رَمَضَانَ وَتَنْكَسِفُ الشَّمْسُ فِي النِّصْفِ مِنْهُ
refs.en: “For our Mahdi there are two signs which have never occurred since the creation of the heavens and the earth: the moon will be eclipsed on the first night (of its eclipse nights) in Ramadan, and the sun will be eclipsed in the middle (of its eclipse days) of it.”

t11.use: Explain the 13th and 28th dates first, then give the 1894 dates. Ask: “Who else claimed to be the Mahdi when this happened?”
t11.gr:
• لِأَوَّلِ لَيْلَةٍ — “on the first night” of the nights on which a lunar eclipse can happen (13th), since the moon of the 1st night is a hilal and is not called qamar.
• فِي النِّصْفِ مِنْهُ — in the middle of the possible solar-eclipse days (28th).

obj.a: Daraqutni is among the greatest hadith critics; and the sign’s fulfilment in its exact form, while a claimant was present, confirms it. A false report would not be fulfilled so precisely.

refs.ar: وَمُبَشِّرًا بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِي مِن بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ ۖ فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُم بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ قَالُوا هَٰذَا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ
refs.en: “…and giving glad tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, his name being Ahmad. But when he came to them with clear proofs, they said, ‘This is clear magic.’”

t12.use: Mention his actual name was Ahmad (Ghulam was a family prefix) and his father named a village Ahmadabad after him.

obj.o: “‘Lamma ja’ahum’ is past tense, so it already happened.”
obj.a: Prophecies in the Quran are often stated in the past tense for certainty. Ahmadis also accept the Holy Prophet (sa) as Ahmad; the Promised Messiah is a reflection of him (see the site card on Ahmad).

refs.ar: وَلَيُتْرَكَنَّ الْقِلَاصُ فَلَا يُسْعَى عَلَيْهَا
refs.en: “…and young she-camels will be abandoned and no one will ride them.”
refs.cite: Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Iman (descent of Jesus son of Mary)

refs.ar: وَإِذَا الْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ
refs.en: “And when the she-camels, ten months pregnant, are abandoned.”

t13.use: Short sign for any audience: camels replaced by railways — including the Hejaz railway to Makkah and Madinah.

refs.ar: لَا الْمَهْدِيُّ إِلَّا عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ
refs.en: “There is no Mahdi except Jesus son of Mary.”
refs.cite: Sunan Ibn Majah, Kitab al-Fitan, Bab Shiddat al-Zaman

refs.ar: يُوشِكُ مَنْ عَاشَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَلْقَى عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ إِمَامًا مَهْدِيًّا وَحَكَمًا عَدْلًا
refs.en: “Whoever of you lives will soon meet Jesus son of Mary as a rightly-guided Imam (Mahdi) and a just arbiter.”

refs.ar: كَيْفَ تَهْلِكُ أُمَّةٌ أَنَا أَوَّلُهَا وَعِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ آخِرُهَا
refs.en: “How can an Ummah perish of which I am the first and Jesus son of Mary the last?”
refs.cite: Mishkat al-Masabih, Kitab al-Manaqib; Kanz al-Ummal; Hujaj al-Kiramah (Nawab Siddiq Hasan Khan)

m1.use: “If the Mahdi were a separate great figure, why did the Prophet (sa) mention only Jesus as the ‘last’ of the Ummah?”

refs.ar: وَأَنزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ
refs.en: “And We sent down iron, wherein is great strength.”

refs.ar: يَا بَنِي آدَمَ قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاسًا
refs.en: “O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing.”

refs.ar: قَدْ أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكُمْ ذِكْرًا ۝ رَّسُولًا
refs.en: “Allah has indeed sent down to you a Reminder — a Messenger.”

refs.ar: كَانَ إِذَا نَزَلَ مَنْزِلًا فِي سَفَرٍ لَمْ يَرْتَحِلْ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ فِيهِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ
refs.en: “When he (the Prophet) stopped (nazala) at a place on a journey, he would not leave until he had prayed two rak’ahs there.”
refs.cite: Kanz al-Ummal, Kitab al-Shama’il, Adab al-Safar

refs.ar: لَتَنْزِلَنَّ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أُمَّتِي أَرْضًا يُقَالُ لَهَا الْبَصْرَةُ
refs.en: “A group of my Ummah will surely settle (tanzilanna) in a land called Basra.”

m2.use: “Did iron and cattle fall from the sky? Then why must ‘nuzul’ mean that for the Messiah?”
m2.gr:
• نَزَلَ / أَنْزَلَ: to come down, to alight, to settle at a place — used for honour and for things that come by Allah’s decree, not only for physical descent. Bukhari uses “nuzul” in chapter titles for a person settling somewhere (see site card).
• The authentic hadith says only “when the son of Mary descends among you” — the words “from heaven” are not in Bukhari or Muslim.

refs.ar: إِنَّكُنَّ لَأَنْتُنَّ صَوَاحِبُ يُوسُفَ
refs.en: “You are indeed like the women (companions) of Yusuf.”
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Adhan, Bab Ahl al-‘Ilm wal-Fadl Ahaqq bil-Imamah

refs.ar: وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ... وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرَانَ الَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِنَا
refs.en: “And Allah sets forth for those who believe the example of… Mary, daughter of ‘Imran, who guarded her chastity — so We breathed into him of Our Spirit.” — believers can be like Mary, and from that state a “son of Mary” is born spiritually.

m3.use: With Christians: Elijah came as John the Baptist (Matthew 11:14). With Muslims: “sawahib Yusuf” in Bukhari.

refs.ar: وَرَسُولًا إِلَىٰ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ
refs.en: “And (he will be) a Messenger to the Children of Israel.”

refs.ar: فَيُمْسِكُ الَّتِي قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا الْمَوْتَ
refs.en: “…then He retains those (souls) on which He has decreed death.”

refs.ar: كُنتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ
refs.en: “You are the best people raised for mankind.”

m4.use: “Does the Ummah of the greatest prophet need to import a prophet from Bani Israel?”

refs.ar: فَإِذَا رَجُلٌ آدَمُ كَأَحْسَنِ مَا يُرَى مِنْ أُدْمِ الرِّجَالِ
refs.en: The coming Messiah: “a wheat-coloured man, the most handsome of wheat-coloured men one can see.”

refs.ar: آدَمُ ضَرْبٌ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ
refs.en: The Mahdi: “wheat-coloured, of medium build.”

refs.ar: فَأَمَّا عِيسَى فَأَحْمَرُ جَعْدٌ
refs.en: Jesus (whom he saw at the Mi’raj with Moses and Abraham): “reddish, with curly hair.”

m5.use: Draw two columns: Jesus of Nazareth (red, curly) vs coming Messiah (wheat-coloured, straight hair) = Mahdi (wheat-coloured).

refs.ar: يُدْفَنُ مَعِي فِي قَبْرِي
refs.en: “He will be buried with me in my grave.”
refs.cite: Mishkat al-Masabih, Kitab al-Fitan, Bab Nuzul ‘Isa (from Ibn al-Jawzi, Kitab al-Wafa)

refs.ar: ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ
refs.en: “Then He causes him to die and assigns a grave to him.”

m6.use: Ask: “Can anyone open the Prophet’s grave? Then the meaning is spiritual nearness” — and read 80:22.

refs.ar: فَذَكَرَ خُرُوجَ الدَّجَّالِ قَالَ: فَأَنْزِلُ فَأَقْتُلُهُ
refs.en: “He mentioned the emergence of the Dajjal, and said: I will descend and kill him.”
refs.cite: Sunan Ibn Majah, Bab Fitnat al-Dajjal wa Khuruj ‘Isa (mawquf)

m7.use: Say: “This is Ibn Mas’ud’s statement, not the Prophet’s; and at the Mi’raj Jesus was among the dead prophets with Yahya.”

refs.ar: فَيَكْسِرُ الصَّلِيبَ وَيَقْتُلُ الْخِنْزِيرَ وَيَضَعُ الْجِزْيَةَ
refs.en: “…he will break the cross, kill the swine and abolish the jizya.”
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab Ahadith al-Anbiya, Bab Nuzul ‘Isa

refs.ar: وَيَضَعُ الْحَرْبَ
refs.en: “…and he will put an end to war.”

m8.use: Ask: “Will breaking wooden crosses change anyone’s faith? Proving Jesus didn’t die on the cross breaks Christianity’s foundation.”

refs.ar: فَمَن شَرِبَ مِنْهُ فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي
refs.en: “Whoever drinks of it is not of me.”

refs.ar: فَمَن تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي
refs.en: Ibrahim (as): “Whoever follows me is surely of me.”

refs.ar: أَنْتَ مِنِّي وَأَنَا مِنْكَ
refs.en: The Holy Prophet (sa) to Hazrat Ali (ra): “You are from me and I am from you.”
refs.cite: Mishkat al-Masabih, Kitab al-Manaqib, Manaqib Ali

refs.ar: ثَلَاثٌ مَنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِيهِ فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي وَلَا مِنَ اللَّهِ
refs.en: “Whoever lacks three qualities (knowledge, good manners, piety) is neither from me nor from Allah.”

a1.use: Read 14:37 and the hadith about Ali (ra): “Was Ali part of the Prophet’s body?”
a1.gr: • مِن here is for ittisal (connection/nearness), not tab’id (being a part of).

refs.ar: أَنْتَ مِنِّي بِمَنْزِلَةِ وَلَدِي
refs.en: “You are to Me in the position of My son.”
refs.cite: Revelation of the Promised Messiah (as), Haqiqat al-Wahi

refs.ar: فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَذِكْرِكُمْ آبَاءَكُمْ أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْرًا
refs.en: “Remember Allah as you remember your fathers, or even more.”
Shah Waliullah: the word “sons” in earlier scriptures stood for “beloved ones”; later Christians failed to understand this and took sonship literally.

a2.use: Point to the word “bi-manzilati” — a simile, not an identity.

refs.ar: اعْمَلُوا مَا شِئْتُمْ فَقَدْ غَفَرْتُ لَكُمْ
refs.en: About the people of Badr: “Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you.”
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Maghazi (Hadith of Hatib)

refs.en: Sayyid Abdul Qadir Jilani: Allah grants some of His servants the station where “Be” (kun) is given to them by His permission.
refs.cite: Futuh al-Ghayb, Sayyid Abdul Qadir Jilani

a3.use: Explain “qul” is understood before kun fa-yakun; read the Badr hadith “do as you wish” to show it means forgiveness, not licence.

refs.ar: لَوْلَاكَ لَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْأَفْلَاكَ
refs.en: “Were it not for you, I would not have created the heavens.”
refs.cite: Mawdu’at Kabir (Mulla Ali Qari) — said about the Holy Prophet (sa)

refs.en: Peter: “We, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.”

a4.use: Note it was first said of the Holy Prophet (sa); explain ‘new heaven and earth’ in every reformer’s time.

refs.ar: إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ
refs.en: “I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon — I saw them bowing down to me.”

refs.ar: رَأَيْتُنِي فِي الْمَنَامِ عَيْنَ اللَّهِ
refs.en: “I saw myself in a dream as God Himself” — with the interpretation he gave right after it.
refs.cite: A’ina-e-Kamalat-e-Islam, Ruhani Khaza’in vol. 5, p. 564; Kitab al-Bariyya, RK vol. 13

a5.use: Always show the full passage including his own explanation.

refs.ar: وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ ... وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرَانَ الَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِنَا
refs.en: “And Allah sets forth for the believers the example of the wife of Pharaoh… and Mary, daughter of ‘Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into him of Our Spirit.”

refs.ar: مَا مِنْ مَوْلُودٍ يُولَدُ إِلَّا وَالشَّيْطَانُ يَمَسُّهُ ... غَيْرَ مَرْيَمَ وَابْنِهَا
refs.en: “Every child is touched by Satan at birth except Mary and her son.”
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari; Zamakhshari (Kashshaf): it covers everyone with the qualities of Mary and her son

a6.use: Ask: “Is a man a woman because Allah made Mary an example for male believers?”

refs.ar: تُوبِي تُوبِي فَإِنَّ الْبَلَاءَ عَلَى عَقِبِكِ
refs.en: “Repent, repent (O woman), for calamity is on your progeny.”
refs.cite: Majmu’a Ishtiharat vol. 1, announcement of 15 July 1888

refs.ar: وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ
refs.en: “Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness.”
A warning of punishment (wa’id) can be withheld on repentance, unlike a promise (wa’d). Allah’s promises are unconditional; warnings may be cancelled.
refs.cite: Ruh al-Ma’ani under 8:34 (8:33); hadith of Anas (as quoted in the Pocket Book)

a7.use: Explain the condition (repentance) first; then Ahmad Beg’s death; then Sultan Muhammad’s attitude.

obj.a: The text itself invites Thanaullah to publish it with his reply in his own paper and to write what he wished; the Promised Messiah (as) called it in the manner of Mubahala. Thanaullah refused.

refs.ar: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ ۝ وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّىٰ ... إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَىٰ ۝ صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ
refs.en: “Truly he prospers who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays… This indeed is in the former scriptures — the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.”

g1.use: Start with common ground: the agreement of mankind is itself evidence.

refs.ar: أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ ۖ فَبِهُدَاهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ
refs.en: “These are they whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance.”

g2.use: Court analogy: one who says “I saw” beats one who says “I didn’t see” — thousands of truthful prophets said they spoke with God.

refs.ar: وَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوَّامَةِ
refs.en: “And I call to witness the self-accusing soul.”

refs.ar: أَمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ الْخَالِقُونَ
refs.en: “Were they created from nothing, or are they themselves the creators?”

g3.use: Ask the atheist: “Why does your conscience blame you for lying even when no one knows?”

refs.ar: مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلْقِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ مِن تَفَاوُتٍ ۖ فَارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ هَلْ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورٍ ۝ ثُمَّ ارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ يَنقَلِبْ إِلَيْكَ الْبَصَرُ خَاسِئًا وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ
refs.en: “No incongruity can you see in the creation of the Gracious God. Look again: do you see any flaw? Look again and again; your sight will return to you confused and fatigued.”

g4.use: Use one concrete example (water, sun, the eye) and read 67:4–5: “Look again — do you see any flaw?”

refs.ar: كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَأَغْلِبَنَّ أَنَا وَرُسُلِي
refs.en: “Allah has decreed: Most surely I will prevail, I and My Messengers.”

g5.use: Ask: “Name a prophet who failed. Name a persecutor of prophets who is honoured today.”

refs.ar: ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ
refs.en: “Call on Me; I will answer you.”

refs.ar: وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا
refs.en: “Those who strive in Our path — We will surely guide them in Our ways.”

g6.use: Invite the atheist to the 40-day sincere prayer experiment — it costs nothing and cannot be faked.

refs.ar: لَّا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصَارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الْأَبْصَارَ
refs.en: “Eyes cannot reach Him but He reaches the eyes.”

g7.use: List unseen things they accept (reason, gravity, the mind), then read 6:104.

refs.ar: وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ
refs.en: “And for every people there is a guide.”

g8.use: Answer each objection with one short analogy (doctor, king’s palace, thieves in a state); don’t lecture.

refs.en: “I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.”
“Let the wilderness and the cities thereof lift up their voice, the villages that Kedar doth inhabit: let the inhabitants of the rock (Sela) sing.”
“I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now. Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself.”

refs.ar: الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الرَّسُولَ النَّبِيَّ الْأُمِّيَّ الَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوبًا عِندَهُمْ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنجِيلِ
refs.en: “Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet, the Unlettered one, whom they find mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel which are with them.”

x1.use: Read Deuteronomy 18:18 and ask: “Who was like Moses — a law-giver, ruler, married, died naturally? Jesus or Muhammad?”

refs.en: “Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God.”
“And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.”
“I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.”
“Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.”

refs.ar: مَّا الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ
refs.en: “The Messiah son of Mary was only a Messenger.”

x2.use: Ask the Christian: “Show me one verse where Jesus says ‘I am God, worship me’.” Then read Mark 10:18 and John 17:3.

refs.ar: فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُوا لَهُ سَاجِدِينَ
refs.en: About Adam: “When I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My Spirit, fall down in submission to him.”

refs.ar: إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَىٰ عِندَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ ۖ خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ
refs.en: “The case of Jesus with Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him ‘Be’, and he was.”

x3.use: Ask: “Elijah raised the dead — is he God? Adam had God’s spirit — is he God?”

refs.en: “…he offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared.”
“And Pilate marvelled if he were already dead.”
“Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones… And he took it, and did eat before them.”
“He that is hanged is accursed of God.”

x4.use: Walk through 4 points: prayer heard (Hebrews 5:7), short time on cross, Pilate surprised, ate food after. End with the sign of Jonah.

refs.en: “The soul that sinneth, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father… the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him.”
“Let the wicked forsake his way… and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him… for he will abundantly pardon.”
“For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice.”

refs.ar: وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ
refs.en: “No bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another.”

x5.use: Ask: “Would a just judge hang his innocent son and free the criminals?” Then read Ezekiel 18:20.

refs.ar: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ ۚ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا فِيهِ اخْتِلَافًا كَثِيرًا
refs.en: “Will they not ponder over the Quran? Had it been from anyone other than Allah, they would surely have found in it much contradiction.”
“Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord.” — Jesus quoted this as the first commandment.

refs.ar: لَّقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ ثَالِثُ ثَلَاثَةٍ
refs.en: “They are surely disbelievers who say: Allah is the third of three.”

x6.use: Ask them to find ‘Trinity’ in the Bible; then show 1 John 5:7 is removed in modern translations.

refs.en: “But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak… even that prophet shall die.”
“Ye shall know them by their fruits.”
“From the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away… there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. Blessed is he that waiteth.”
“For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.”

x7.use: For Christians, use their own tests: Deuteronomy 18:20 and ‘by their fruits’ (Matthew 7:16).

“Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown… And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil.”

refs.ar: وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا
refs.en: “We never punish until We have sent a Messenger.”
“But I am a worm, and no man.”

“We had no concern with the padres’ Yasu… they needlessly abused our Prophet (sa) and forced us to show them something of their Yasu.”

refs.ar: وَلَا تَسُبُّوا الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ فَيَسُبُّوا اللَّهَ عَدْوًا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ
refs.en: “Revile not those whom they call upon besides Allah, lest they revile Allah out of spite in ignorance.” — the reply came only after they abused.

refs.en: About Yahya: “We gave him wisdom while yet a child.”

refs.ar: وَقَوْلِهِمْ عَلَىٰ مَرْيَمَ بُهْتَانًا عَظِيمًا
refs.en: “…and their uttering against Mary a grievous calumny.” — the Quran’s praise of Mary answers Jewish slander.

x10.use: Answer with Adam (no father or mother) and Yahya (wisdom as a child).

refs.ar: أَوَمَن كَانَ مَيْتًا فَأَحْيَيْنَاهُ وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُ نُورًا يَمْشِي بِهِ فِي النَّاسِ
refs.en: “Can he who was dead, and We gave him life and made for him a light whereby he walks among men…”

refs.ar: أَنِّي أَخْلُقُ لَكُم مِّنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ فَأَنفُخُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طَيْرًا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ
refs.en: “I will fashion for you out of clay the likeness of a bird; then I will breathe into it and it will become a bird by Allah’s leave.”

refs.ar: اسْتَجِيبُوا لِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ إِذَا دَعَاكُمْ لِمَا يُحْيِيكُمْ
refs.en: “Respond to Allah and the Messenger when he calls you that he may give you life.”

refs.ar: مَنْ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ النَّاسَ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ اللَّهَ
refs.en: “Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah.”

refs.en: “Permission (to fight) is given to those against whom war is made, because they have been wronged.”

refs.en: “And strive against them with it (the Quran) a great striving.”

refs.en: The Messiah “will put an end to war.”

refs.en: “Those who strive in Our path, We will surely guide them in Our ways.”

refs.ar: قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ
refs.en: “Say: Bring your proof if you are truthful.”

refs.en: “There is no people to whom a warner has not been sent.”

refs.ar: وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلَّا كَافَّةً لِّلنَّاسِ
refs.en: “We have not sent you but to all mankind.”

refs.en: “The Dajjal will come out on a white donkey, the distance between whose ears is seventy arm-spans.”

refs.ar: وَإِذَا الْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ ۝ ... وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ ۝ وَإِذَا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ ۝ ... وَإِذَا الصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ
refs.en: “When the she-camels are abandoned… when the seas are made to flow into one another, when people are brought together… when books are spread abroad.”

refs.en: “And the earth brings forth her burdens.”

th4.use: Give modern examples for each verse of al-Takwir (canals, travel, printing).

refs.ar: مَا مِنْ نَبِيٍّ إِلَّا وَقَدْ أَنْذَرَ أُمَّتَهُ الْأَعْوَرَ الْكَذَّابَ
refs.en: “There was no prophet who did not warn his people against the one-eyed liar.”

refs.ar: إِنَّ مَعَهُ جَبَلَ خُبْزٍ وَنَهَرَ مَاءٍ
refs.en: “He will have with him a mountain of bread and a river of water.”

th5.use: Read the first ten verses of al-Kahf (Muslim): protection from the Dajjal is about the ‘son of God’ doctrine.

refs.ar: لَتَتَّبِعُنَّ سَنَنَ مَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكُمْ شِبْرًا بِشِبْرٍ وَذِرَاعًا بِذِرَاعٍ
refs.en: “You will follow the ways of those before you, span by span and cubit by cubit.”

refs.ar: وَإِذَا وَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ
refs.en: “And when the sentence is passed against them, We shall bring forth for them a creature out of the earth which shall wound them.”

refs.ar: يَنْزِلُ عِنْدَ الْمَنَارَةِ الْبَيْضَاءِ شَرْقِيَّ دِمَشْقَ
refs.en: “He will descend at the White Minaret, east of Damascus.”
refs.cite: Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan; Kanz al-Ummal

th6.use: Explain the White Minaret in Qadian (east of Damascus) as a symbol of the Messiah’s light.

refs.ar: لَمْ يَبْقَ مِنَ النُّبُوَّةِ إِلَّا الْمُبَشِّرَاتُ
refs.en: “Nothing remains of prophethood except mubashshirat (glad tidings).”

refs.ar: لَهُمُ الْبُشْرَىٰ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ
refs.en: “For them are glad tidings in the present life and in the Hereafter.”

th7.use: Ask: “Do mubashshirat (true visions) still come? Then the essence of prophethood remains.”

refs.ar: لَوْ كَانَ بَعْدِي نَبِيٌّ لَكَانَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ
refs.en: “If there were to be a prophet after me, it would have been Umar b. al-Khattab.”

refs.ar: وَيُحْصَرُ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ عِيسَى وَأَصْحَابُهُ
refs.en: “And the Prophet of Allah, Jesus, and his companions will be besieged.” — the coming Messiah is called “Nabiullah” four times in this hadith.

th8.use: Note the Messiah is called ‘Nabiullah’ four times in Sahih Muslim — after the Prophet (sa).

refs.ar: إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَا التَّوْرَاةَ فِيهَا هُدًى وَنُورٌ ۚ يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا
refs.en: “Surely We sent down the Torah wherein was guidance and light; by it did the prophets, who were obedient to Us, judge.”

refs.ar: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلْنَا مَعَهُ أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ وَزِيرًا
refs.en: “We gave Moses the Book and appointed with him his brother Aaron as a helper.”

refs.en: “He it is Who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over every other religion.”

refs.ar: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ وَفَرْعُهَا فِي السَّمَاءِ
refs.en: “Do you not see how Allah sets forth the example of a good word? It is like a good tree, whose root is firm and whose branches reach into heaven.”
