refs.ar: وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا
refs.en: “And He has placed the moon therein as a light, and made the sun as a lamp.”

refs.ar: وَدَاعِيًا إِلَى اللَّهِ بِإِذْنِهِ وَسِرَاجًا مُّنِيرًا
refs.en: “…and as a summoner unto Allah by His command, and as a light-giving sun (siraj munir).”

kn2.use: Use the sun and moon image — easy to remember and explain.

refs.ar: فَإِنِّي آخِرُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ وَإِنَّ مَسْجِدِي آخِرُ الْمَسَاجِدِ
refs.en: “I am the last of the prophets, and my mosque is the last of the mosques.”
refs.cite: Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Hajj (Fadl al-Salat bi-Masjidai Makkah wal-Madinah)

kn3.use: Quote “my mosque is the last mosque” (Muslim) — mosques are still built.
kn3.gr: • آخِر in such phrases expresses completion and excellence: the last mosque = the last mosque of a law-bearing prophet. The same hadith links “last prophet” to “last mosque” — they must be understood the same way.

refs.ar: تَكُونُ النُّبُوَّةُ فِيكُمْ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ أَنْ تَكُونَ ... ثُمَّ تَكُونُ خِلَافَةٌ عَلَى مِنْهَاجِ النُّبُوَّةِ ... ثُمَّ تَكُونُ مُلْكًا عَاضًّا ... ثُمَّ تَكُونُ مُلْكًا جَبْرِيَّةً ... ثُمَّ تَكُونُ خِلَافَةٌ عَلَى مِنْهَاجِ النُّبُوَّةِ ثُمَّ سَكَتَ
refs.en: “Prophethood will remain among you as long as Allah wills… then Khilafat on the precept of prophethood… then biting kingship… then tyrannical kingship… then Khilafat on the precept of prophethood. Then he fell silent.”
refs.cite: Musnad Ahmad (hadith of Hudhayfah); Mishkat al-Masabih, Kitab al-Riqaq

kn4.use: Read the Hudhayfah hadith; ask: “Khilafat on the precept of prophethood after kingship — following which prophet?”

refs.ar: لَا تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى يُبْعَثَ دَجَّالُونَ كَذَّابُونَ قَرِيبٌ مِنْ ثَلَاثِينَ كُلُّهُمْ يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ
refs.en: “The Hour will not come until nearly thirty great liars appear, each claiming to be the Messenger of Allah.”
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Manaqib; Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan

kn5.use: Point out the number thirty means not every claimant is false.

refs.ar: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ
refs.en: “There is none worthy of worship except Allah; Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.”

refs.ar: مَنْ صَلَّى صَلَاتَنَا وَاسْتَقْبَلَ قِبْلَتَنَا وَأَكَلَ ذَبِيحَتَنَا فَذَلِكَ الْمُسْلِمُ
refs.en: “Whoever prays our prayer, faces our qibla and eats our slaughtered animals is a Muslim.”

kn6.use: Simply recite the Kalima and ask: “What is different?”

refs.en: “When this communication is abundant with someone, he is called a muhaddath.”
refs.cite: Maktubat Imam Rabbani (Mujaddid Alf Thani), vol. 2, letter 51 (as quoted)

refs.ar: لَقَدْ كَانَ فِيمَا قَبْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْأُمَمِ مُحَدَّثُونَ فَإِنْ يَكُ فِي أُمَّتِي أَحَدٌ فَإِنَّهُ عُمَرُ
refs.en: “Among the nations before you there were people who were spoken to (muhaddathun); if there is one in my Ummah, it is Umar.”

kn7.use: Quote Mujaddid Alf Thani — respected by Deobandis and Barelvis alike.

refs.ar: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَقَفَّيْنَا مِن بَعْدِهِ بِالرُّسُلِ
refs.en: “And verily We gave Moses the Book and caused Messengers to follow in his footsteps after him.”
Maulana Maududi observed that people outwardly reject any mention of prophethood but inwardly long for a figure no less than a prophet.
refs.cite: Tarjuman al-Quran (as quoted in the book)

kn8.use: Ask: “Did Moses’ followers have prophets after him? Is the Holy Prophet (sa) less?”

refs.ar: أَفَإِن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ
refs.en: “If then you die, shall they live on for ever?”

hb1.use: Open a conversation with these three reasons to show why it matters.

refs.ar: وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا الْمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ
refs.en: “And their saying, ‘We did kill the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah’, whereas they slew him not, nor did they bring about his death on the cross.”
“He that is hanged is accursed of God.”

hb2.use: Explain the Jews’ claim of an accursed death (Deut. 21:23).

refs.ar: وَلَٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ ۚ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِّنْهُ
refs.en: “…but he was made to appear to them like one (crucified); and those who differ therein are certainly in a state of doubt about it.”

hb3.use: Point to the passive verb: no one else is mentioned as being made to look like him.
hb3.gr:
• شُبِّهَ (Form II passive, madi majhul): the naa’ib al-fa’il (deputy subject) must be found in the context. The only candidates are Jesus himself or “the matter” — not an unmentioned third person.
• The verse continues: “those who differ about it are in doubt” — the event was confusing, not a clean substitution.

refs.ar: إِنَّهُ قَدْ سَبَقَ الْقَوْلُ مِنِّي أَنَّهُمْ لَا يُرْجَعُونَ
refs.en: “It has already been decreed by Me that they shall not be returned.”
refs.cite: Jami’ al-Tirmidhi, Kitab Tafsir al-Quran (Al Imran); Sunan Ibn Majah

hb4.use: Tell the story of Jabir’s father — vivid and easy to remember.

refs.ar: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ
refs.en: “And Muhammad is only a Messenger; all Messengers have passed away before him.”

hb5.use: Explain how Christian converts influenced later ideas; the Companions agreed all prophets had died.

refs.ar: قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّي هَلْ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرًا رَّسُولًا
refs.en: “Say: Holy is my Lord! I am but a man sent as a Messenger.”

hb6.use: Use it with Muslims: “Your belief hands Christians their best argument.”

refs.ar: وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِّلسَّاعَةِ فَلَا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا وَاتَّبِعُونِ ۚ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ
refs.en: “And surely he/it is a sign of the Hour. So have no doubt about it, and follow me. This is the right path.”

refs.ar: وَقِيلَ: إِنَّ مَعْنَاهُ أَنَّ الْقُرْآنَ لَدَلِيلٌ لِلسَّاعَةِ لِأَنَّهُ آخِرُ الْكُتُبِ
refs.en: “It is said: it means the Quran is a proof of the Hour, because it is the last Book.”
refs.cite: Tafsir Majma’ al-Bayan; also Jami’ al-Bayan

u11.use: Ask: “If the sign of the Hour is 2,000 years away, why tell the Prophet’s listeners ‘do not doubt it’ and ‘follow me’?” Then show the tafsirs that say it refers to the Quran.
u11.gr:
• إِنَّهُ — the pronoun’s antecedent (marji’) is disputed; the Quran is mentioned in the surrounding verses.
• وَاتَّبِعُونِ — “follow ME”: the imperative points to the Holy Prophet (sa).

refs.ar: وَإِن مِّنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ إِلَّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ
refs.en: “And there is none among the People of the Book but will believe in it before his death.”

u12.use: Ask: “Did every Jew of the last 2,000 years believe in Jesus before dying? Will the 70,000 with the Dajjal?” Then give the meaning: belief about his death on the cross.
u12.gr: • Abu Hurairah’s (ra) reading of this verse in Bukhari is his own ijtihad, not a saying of the Prophet (sa).

refs.ar: وَيُكَلِّمُ النَّاسَ فِي الْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًا وَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ
refs.en: “And he shall speak to the people in the cradle and when of middle age, and he shall be of the righteous.”

u13.use: Short: “Kahl starts around 30; he lived to 120 — so he spoke in middle age long ago. No need to return for that.”
u13.gr: • كَهْل in the lexicons covers roughly the thirties onward (Majma’ Bihar al-Anwar).

obj.o: “‘He will teach him the Book and Wisdom’ (3:49) means the Quran, so he must return to learn it.”
obj.a: The Quran also says “We gave the family of Abraham the Book and Wisdom” (4:55). Imam Razi: here “the Book” means writing and “Wisdom” means knowledge and good morals.

refs.ar: وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا
refs.en: “…and will clear you of (the charges of) those who disbelieve.”

refs.ar: إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنكُمُ الرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمْ تَطْهِيرًا
refs.en: “Allah only wishes to remove all impurity from you, O people of the household, and to purify you completely.”

u14.use: Explain purification = clearing his name from false charges; cite 33:34 for the Ahl al-Bayt. Then: wounds at Uhud did not make the Prophet (sa) less honoured.

obj.o: “Hanging on the cross is against being ‘honoured (wajih) in this world’.”
obj.a: Being KILLED on the cross would make him ‘accursed’ (Deut. 21:23). Merely being hung and wounded does not — the Holy Prophet (sa) was wounded and lost a tooth at Uhud, yet he is the most honoured.

refs.en: Imam Suyuti quotes the same narration from Bayhaqi (al-Asma’ wal-Sifat) without the words “min al-sama’”.
Yunus b. Yazid al-Ayli: “he occasionally did tadlis.”

u15.use: If someone quotes “min al-sama’”, ask them to show it in Bukhari or Muslim — it isn’t there; then show Suyuti quoting Bayhaqi without it.

refs.ar: إِنَّ عِيسَى لَمْ يَمُتْ
refs.en: “Jesus has not died.”
refs.cite: Tafsir Ibn Jarir (Jami’ al-Bayan) — mursal of Hasan Basri

refs.en: “People avoid his narrations through Abu Ja’far, because there is much confusion in them.”
refs.cite: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, Ibn Hajar, under Rabi’ b. Anas

u16.use: Ask for the chain: it is mursal from Hasan Basri with weak narrators — it cannot override Quran 3:145 and 5:118.

refs.en: “I am the Black Stone placed on earth, and people will be blessed by touching it.” — his own explanation of the dream.
refs.cite: Writings of the Promised Messiah (as), quoted in the Pocket Book

refs.ar: إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا
refs.en: Yusuf’s dream of stars bowing — symbolic, not literal.

a9.use: Say it was a dream he himself interpreted; compare Yusuf’s dream of stars bowing.

refs.ar: وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِ
refs.en: “We have not sent any Messenger except with the language of his people.”
Examples of the English revelations: “Then will you go to Amritsar”; “Words of God cannot exchange.”

a10.use: Read 14:5 and note the Quran’s own change of person (iltifat) in al-Fatiha.

refs.ar: فَأَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهَا رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا
refs.en: “We sent to her Our angel, and he appeared to her in the form of a perfect man.”

a11.use: Correct the quote first: it was a dream of an angel giving a descriptive name, not a revelation “Tichi Tichi”.

refs.ar: قَالَ يَا نُوحُ إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ ۖ إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَالِحٍ
refs.en: “He said: O Noah, he is not of your family; he is (one of) unrighteous conduct.”

refs.ar: إِنِّي أُرِيتُ لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ ثُمَّ أُنْسِيتُهَا
refs.en: “I was shown Laylat al-Qadr, then I was made to forget it.”
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab Fadl Laylat al-Qadr

refs.ar: فَيَنسَخُ اللَّهُ مَا يُلْقِي الشَّيْطَانُ ثُمَّ يُحْكِمُ اللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ
refs.en: “Allah removes what Satan casts, then Allah firmly establishes His Signs.”

a12.use: Use Noah’s son (11:47) and the forgotten date of Laylat al-Qadr: prophets interpret details by ijtihad.

refs.en: “Hosanna to the son of David” — hosanna means “save, we pray.”

refs.ar: وَأُحْيِي الْمَوْتَىٰ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ
refs.en: Jesus: “…and I quicken the dead by Allah’s leave.”

a13.use: Translate the words (Hosanna = save, we pray) and link to Jesus’ own words.

refs.en: Revelations about his approaching death published in Al-Wasiyyat (December 1905), two and a half years before his death.
Announcement “Tabsirah” (5 November 1907) in reply to Abdul Hakim.

a14.use: Ask: “Abdul Hakim changed his date three times — which one was the prophecy?”

refs.en: “Your age will be eighty years, or a few years more or less.”
refs.cite: Haqiqat al-Wahi, Ruhani Khaza’in vol. 22, p. 100 (revelation)

refs.ar: ثَمَانِينَ حَوْلًا أَوْ قَرِيبًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ
refs.en: “Eighty years, or close to that.”

a15.use: Explain the revelation allowed “a few years less or more”.

refs.en: The prophecy contained the condition: “provided he does not turn towards the truth.”
“Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not.”
“Moreover I call God for a record upon my soul…”
“For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife.”

a16.use: Emphasise the condition “unless he turns to the truth” and Atham’s refusal to swear.

refs.en: “This boy’s birth has been postponed, because I prayed: My Lord, delay this time.”
Vision of 19 February 1906 regarding Manzur Muhammad’s son.

a17.use: Explain postponement through prayer and that the qualities were fulfilled in the Musleh Mau’ud.

refs.ar: إِنِّي أُحَافِظُ كُلَّ مَنْ فِي الدَّارِ
refs.en: “I will protect all who are within this house.”

refs.ar: إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَامٍ نَافِلَةً لَّكَ
refs.en: “We give you glad tidings of a boy as a gift for you (a grandson).”

a18.use: Read the exact revelation (protection of his house; Qadian saved from destructive plague) before discussing cases.

refs.ar: إِنَّ مِنَ الشِّعْرِ لَحِكْمَةً
refs.en: “Some poetry is wisdom.”

refs.ar: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا
refs.en: “…except those who believe and do good works and remember Allah much.” (exception for believing poets)
Dhul-Yadayn asked “Has the prayer been shortened or did you forget?” — the Prophet (sa) had prayed two rak’ahs by forgetfulness.

a19.use: Ask for the original book and page; most ‘wrong references’ are edition differences or Christian Bible changes.

refs.en: “Where I have denied prophethood, it is only in the sense that I am not an independent bringer of law… and I am a prophet in the sense that I receive abundant communication from God.”
refs.cite: Ek Ghalati ka Izala, Ruhani Khaza’in vol. 18

refs.ar: لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّينِ
refs.en: “There is no compulsion in religion.”

a20.use: Define terms first: law-bearing vs ummati prophet. Most ‘contradictions’ vanish.

refs.ar: فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ الْكَلْبِ
refs.en: “His case is like that of a dog.”

refs.ar: عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ زَنِيمٍ
refs.en: “Cruel, and besides, of doubtful birth.”
“Strong replies to harsh attacks in debate are a wise strategy.”
refs.cite: Kitab al-Bariyya, Ruhani Khaza’in vol. 13; Izala-e-Auham

a21.use: Show the Quran’s own strong words (7:177, 68:14) and explain baghaya = rebellious.

refs.ar: إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ بِالطَّاعُونِ بِأَرْضٍ فَلَا تَدْخُلُوهَا وَإِذَا وَقَعَ بِأَرْضٍ وَأَنْتُمْ بِهَا فَلَا تَخْرُجُوا مِنْهَا
refs.en: “If you hear of plague in a land, do not enter it; if it breaks out in a land where you are, do not leave it.”

refs.ar: إِنِّي أَسْقُطُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَأُصِيبُهُ
refs.en: Revelation at Mubarak Ahmad’s birth (foretelling his early death).
refs.cite: Tiryaq al-Qulub, Ruhani Khaza’in vol. 15, p. 213; Tadhkirah

a22.use: Read the Bukhari plague hadith; his instruction matched it exactly.

refs.en: “After God, I am drunk with love of Muhammad; if this is disbelief, by God I am the greatest disbeliever.”

refs.ar: أَلَا وَمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَنْظُرَ إِلَى مُحَمَّدٍ ... فَهَا أَنَا ذَا مُحَمَّدٌ
refs.en: The Mahdi will say: “Whoever wishes to see Muhammad… here I am, Muhammad.”
“I am Adam, I am Noah, I am Abraham… every prophet’s quality must be found in me.”
refs.cite: Tatimma Haqiqat al-Wahi, Ruhani Khaza’in vol. 22

p1.use: Quote his verse of love for the Holy Prophet (sa) and his title ‘ghulam’.

refs.en: Differences on the Mahdi’s birthplace and lineage are recorded by Nawab Siddiq Hasan Khan and Nawab Nurul Hasan Khan.
refs.cite: Hujaj al-Kiramah, p. 356–358; Iqtirab al-Sa’ah, p. 162

refs.ar: سَلْمَانُ مِنَّا أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ
refs.en: “Salman (the Persian) is from us, the people of the house.”

p2.use: Show that the narrations about the Mahdi’s lineage and birthplace contradict each other.

refs.ar: وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا
refs.en: “Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by people who can find a way to it.”
The Prophet (sa) saw in a dream a man circumambulating the Ka’bah — it was said “this is the Dajjal”.
refs.cite: Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Iman (Bab al-Masih ibn Maryam wal-Masih al-Dajjal)

p3.use: Read 3:98 — Hajj requires a safe route; fatwas of death made it unsafe.

refs.ar: بَيْنَ مَهْرُودَتَيْنِ
refs.en: “…between two yellow garments.”
The Prophet (sa) allowed Zubair and ‘Abd al-Rahman b. ‘Awf to wear silk because of an itch.

p4.use: Mention the hadith of the Messiah’s ‘two yellow sheets’ (two illnesses).

refs.ar: فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ
refs.en: “Whoever of you is sick or on a journey shall fast the same number of other days.”
The Prophet (sa) fasted until he reached ‘Usfan, then called for water and broke his fast publicly.

refs.ar: تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَأَنفُسِكُمْ
refs.en: “Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your persons.”

p5.use: Point to the Quran’s and Prophet’s own practice for each objection (Umm Haram, ‘Usfan).

refs.en: “Prophets are buried where they die” — Tirmidhi calls it gharib; its narrator ‘Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Bakr al-Mulayki is weak.
The Prophet’s (sa) fever in his last illness was twice as severe as any man’s.

p6.use: Ask: “Does illness at death disprove a saint? Then why the Prophet’s severe fever?”

refs.ar: مَنْ قَالَ لِأَخِيهِ يَا كَافِرُ فَقَدْ بَاءَ بِهَا أَحَدُهُمَا
refs.en: “Whoever calls his brother ‘O kafir’, it returns to one of them.”
“The denial of the Promised Messiah… is not in itself disbelief in the sense of leaving Islam, but because it is denial of the Holy Prophet’s (sa) prophecy…”
refs.cite: Haqiqat al-Wahi, Ruhani Khaza’in vol. 22, p. 168

p7.use: Ask: “Who issued the first fatwa of kufr?” Then show the sects’ fatwas against each other.

refs.en: Ahrar leaders’ statements against Quaid-e-Azam and Pakistan, quoted from contemporary papers (Zamindar, Ihsan).

p8.use: Show the Ahrar’s statements against Quaid-e-Azam and Pakistan.

refs.en: “Ibrahim did not lie except three times…” — explained as statements with a hidden true meaning.
refs.cite: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab Ahadith al-Anbiya; Jami’ al-Tirmidhi

refs.ar: وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَّبِيًّا
refs.en: “And relate the story of Abraham; he was a truthful man and a Prophet.”

p9.use: Show that Ahmadis defend the innocence of all prophets.

refs.ar: قُل لَّئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الْإِنسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلَىٰ أَن يَأْتُوا بِمِثْلِ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنِ لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ
refs.en: “Say: If men and jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Quran, they could not produce the like of it.”
